documents.title: H&P - Admission, Community-Acquired Pneumonia
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time seen: 21:40, HD1
Chief complaint: cough and shortness of breath x 4 days
HPI:
84 yo female with productive cough, subjective fevers, and progressive dyspnea over 4 days.
Sputum described as yellow-green, small volume. Pleuritic right-sided chest discomfort with cough.
Decreased appetite x 2 days, fatigued, one episode of confusion noted by daughter this morning that cleared.
Prior antibiotic: leftover amoxicillin started at home yesterday; unclear number of doses. No improvement.
No sick contacts. No recent travel. No hemoptysis. No leg swelling or orthopnea.
Presented to ED at 18:20 by daughter for worsening work of breathing.
ED course:
Triage vitals: T 38.4 C, HR 104, BP 128/72, respiratory rate 24 at triage, SpO2 87% on RA at triage.
Placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%. Work of breathing improved.
Repeat at 4 hours: HR 92, BP 124/70, respiratory rate 20 at 4 hours, SpO2 94% on 3L NC.
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV once in the ED plus azithromycin 500 mg IV.
Blood cultures x2 drawn prior to antibiotics. Resp viral panel sent.
Past medical history:
Hypertension, osteoarthritis, hypothyroidism, remote cholecystectomy, mild CKD stage 3a.
Home medications:
Amlodipine 5 mg daily, levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, acetaminophen 650 mg PRN, vitamin D 1000 units daily.
Allergies: sulfa - rash.
Social: lives alone in 1-story home, daughter nearby and checks daily. Never smoker. No alcohol.
Functional: independent with ADLs, uses cane outdoors.
ROS: positive for cough, dyspnea, fever, fatigue, poor appetite. Negative for vomiting, dysuria, rash, calf pain.
Physical exam:
Gen: elderly female, mildly tachypneic at rest, speaking in short phrases.
Vitals on floor 21:35: T 37.9, HR 94, BP 130/74, RR 20, SpO2 93% on 3L NC.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no JVD.
Lungs: crackles right base with decreased breath sounds, no wheeze, no dullness appreciated on left.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no peripheral edema.
Abd: soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds.
Neuro: alert, oriented to person and place, slow to state month. Moves all extremities.
Skin: warm, dry, no rash.
Labs:
WBC 15.6 with 84% neutrophils, Hgb 11.8, Plt 244.
Na 134, K 4.1, Cl 99, CO2 24, BUN 32, Cr 1.24, glucose 118.
Lactate 1.6. Procalcitonin 0.9.
Chest x-ray: patchy right lower lobe infiltrate, no effusion.
Assessment:
84 yo female with community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe, with hypoxemic respiratory insufficiency.
CURB-65 of 3 (age >=65, confusion, BUN >19) - admit to medical floor, telemetry.
Plan:
1. Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV q24h and azithromycin 500 mg IV daily.
2. O2 via NC, titrate to SpO2 92-96%, wean as tolerated.
3. Incentive spirometry q1h while awake, out of bed to chair with assist.
4. Follow blood cultures, resp viral panel, sputum gram stain and culture.
5. Antipyretics PRN, monitor mental status, delirium precautions.
6. Hold amlodipine if soft pressures; continue levothyroxine.
7. Trend CBC, BMP in AM. Daily weights.
8. Diet: regular, encourage PO intake.
9. Code status: full, discussed with pt and daughter at bedside.
10. Anticipate transition to oral therapy once afebrile and tolerating diet.
Attending notified 21:55, agrees with plan.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:35
Subjective:
Pt reports cough improved overnight, slept in 3 hour stretches. Ate most of breakfast this morning.
No chest pain, no new confusion. Daughter at bedside.
Overnight vitals: Tmax 37.8 at 02:10, HR 84-96, BP 126/70 to 138/78, RR 18-20.
SpO2 92-94%; still on 3L NC on hospital day 2.
Exam:
Gen: elderly female, comfortable, conversant, oriented x3 today.
Lungs: right basilar crackles persist, air entry improved, no wheeze.
CV: RRR, no murmur. Ext: no edema.
Abd: soft, nontender.
Labs this AM:
WBC 12.4 (down from 15.6), Hgb 11.5, Plt 238.
Blood cultures no growth to date at 12 hours. Resp viral panel negative.
Assessment:
Right lower lobe community-acquired pneumonia, clinically improving. Afebrile since 02:10, tolerating oral diet.
Plan:
1. Pt received ceftriaxone 1 g IV once in the ED; tolerating oral diet and switched to oral cefpodoxime the next morning - cefpodoxime 200 mg PO BID started today.
2. Continue azithromycin, transition to PO 500 mg daily.
3. Continue O2 3L NC, begin wean trials with ambulation this afternoon.
4. Incentive spirometry q1h awake, up to chair for all meals.
5. PT eval for gait and safety prior to discharge.
6. Repeat pulse ox on room air with ambulation later today.
7. Continue home levothyroxine and amlodipine.
8. Anticipate discharge tomorrow if oxygen requirement resolves.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 15:50 - interval afternoon note
Subjective:
Pt up in chair, cough less frequent and more productive. Ate full lunch. No dyspnea at rest.
Denies chest pain, dizziness, or nausea. States she feels better than yesterday.
Oxygen: weaned to 2L NC at 13:00 with SpO2 94%. Ambulation trial with PT at 14:40 on room air, SpO2 nadir 91%, recovered to 94% at rest.
Currently 1L NC, SpO2 95%.
Exam:
Gen: no distress, speaking full sentences.
Lungs: scattered right base crackles, reduced from AM, no accessory muscle use.
CV: RRR. Ext: warm, no edema.
Neuro: alert and oriented x3, no confusion.
Tolerated first two doses of oral cefpodoxime without nausea. PO azithromycin given at 10:00.
Blood cultures remain no growth at 20 hours. Sputum culture: mixed respiratory flora, no predominant organism.
Assessment:
CAP improving on oral therapy, oxygen requirement declining, mentation back to baseline.
Plan:
1. Continue cefpodoxime 200 mg PO BID and azithromycin 500 mg PO daily.
2. Trial off oxygen overnight with continuous pulse ox; goal SpO2 >=92% on RA.
3. Continue incentive spirometry and ambulation TID with assist.
4. PT recommends cane, no further inpatient needs if RA maintained.
5. Recheck ambulatory saturation in AM.
6. Discharge planning with daughter, target tomorrow.
7. Continue levothyroxine, amlodipine, acetaminophen PRN.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD3
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Discharge time: 12:15, HD3. Length of stay 3 days.
Discharge diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe.
Secondary: hypertension, hypothyroidism, CKD stage 3a.
Brief hospital course:
84 yo female presented with 4 days of productive cough, fever, and dyspnea, with transient confusion.
Prior antibiotic: leftover amoxicillin started at home yesterday; unclear number of doses, taken prior to arrival without improvement.
At triage SpO2 87% on RA at triage; placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%. Respiratory rate 24 at triage, 20 at 4 hours.
Chest x-ray: patchy right lower lobe infiltrate, no effusion.
CURB-65 of 3 on admission; admitted to medical floor on telemetry.
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV once in the ED; tolerating oral diet and switched to oral cefpodoxime the next morning, with azithromycin transitioned to PO the same day.
Still on 3L NC on hospital day 2 in the morning, weaned through the afternoon and maintained on room air overnight.
Afebrile since HD2 02:10. WBC fell from 15.6 to 12.4 to 9.8 on HD3.
Blood cultures x2 no growth at discharge. Resp viral panel negative. Sputum culture with mixed respiratory flora.
Discharge vitals 09:40: T 36.9, HR 78, BP 128/74, RR 18, SpO2 95% on room air; ambulatory saturation 93% on RA.
Discharge exam: alert and oriented x3, mild residual right basilar crackles, no accessory muscle use, no edema.
Discharge medications:
Cefpodoxime 200 mg PO BID to complete a 5 day total course - 3 days remaining.
Azithromycin 500 mg PO daily - 2 days remaining.
Levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, vitamin D 1000 units daily, acetaminophen 650 mg q6h PRN.
Instructions:
Continue incentive spirometry 10 times per hour while awake for 1 week.
Increase activity gradually; use cane for walking outdoors.
Push oral fluids and small frequent meals.
Return precautions: fever >38.3, worsening shortness of breath, confusion, chest pain, or inability to keep down medication.
Follow-up:
Primary care in 5 to 7 days for symptom check and repeat exam.
Repeat chest imaging in 6 to 8 weeks to confirm radiographic resolution.
Pneumococcal and influenza vaccination status to be reviewed as outpatient.
Daughter present for discharge teaching, verbalized understanding of medication schedule.
Condition at discharge: stable, improved.
Disposition: home with daughter checking daily.
